title: Python: resolveStarAttribute picks the last of two conditional stars alone: m.f() gives b.f where Python allows a.f or b.f (split from GCLI-125)
description: Split out of GCLI-125 by the leader's ruling (do not widen GCLI-125). Input: a.py and b.py each def f; m.py is 'try: from a import *' / 'except ImportError: from b import *'; app.py 'import m; m.f()'. origin/dev (3d3986b) gives ONE edge to b.f (unflagged) for the attribute form; Python allows a.f or b.f. A WRONG edge (a single unflagged edge where Python allows two), not a lost one. The bare form 'from m import f; f()' is already right: it gives a.f and b.f, each multiplyBound. Cause: resolveStarAttribute (src/python/calls.ts) walks stars last to first, ignores a star's condition (the known gap its doc comment names), so the last complete star that exports the name decides alone. Fix shape: a conditional last star with an earlier star that could export the name is a refusal (or alternatives, each multiplyBound); same may-skip rule GCLI-125 applies in starOverride. Wrong-edge class: for the leader to route to opum-doc for the (a49) item 7 hold-list decision.

acceptanceCriteria.text: the reproducing input gives alternatives each multiplyBound or no edge, never b.f alone, red before and green after, with callees pinned and the full bin delta
twins: a single unconditional star keeps deciding alone; a conditional lone star keeps deciding (it is the only way the name binds)
a mutant that restores the last-star-decides rule is observed red
the five-pin corpus diff against dev is script-asserted with every moved site named; any in-repo edge created or removed comes to opum-doc before the clear
